item.title: Researchers trick GitHub's AI agent into leaking private repositories, exposing security risks [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Security researchers demonstrated a method to manipulate GitHub's AI agent, causing it to leak information from private repositories. This finding highlights potential vulnerabilities in AI-powered code assistance tools that could expose sensitive data. The researchers detailed their approach and the implications for identity and access management (IAM) in AI systems, emphasizing the need for improved safeguards to prevent unauthorized data disclosure through AI agents.

item.title: ZML releases LLMD alpha, a cross-platform LLM inference server supporting NVIDIA, AMD, Google TPU, Intel, and Apple Metal architectures with modern serving features [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: ZML has launched LLMD alpha, a self-contained inference server that runs large language models like LLaMa, Gemma, Qwen, and Mistral across five hardware architectures including NVIDIA CUDA, AMD ROCm, Google TPU, Intel oneAPI, and Apple Metal. The server supports features such as continuous batching, paged attention, tensor parallel sharding, prefix caching, and tool calling, and exposes metrics in Prometheus format. LLMD alpha includes native support for loading models directly from HuggingFace, S3, and Google Cloud Storage without prior downloading, using ZML's virtual file system. It also introduces DFlash speculative decoding for certain models, which can speed up token processing by up to 10 times. The server ships with optimized Docker images tailored for each platform, including built-in CUDA compatibility and automatic tensor parallel sharding across devices. LLMD runs on ZML's own ML framework built with Zig, MLIR, and OpenXLA, providing predictable latency and a Python-free execution path.

item.title: Rowboat launches open-source, local-first desktop AI coworker with integrated work surfaces and knowledge graph for Mac, Windows, and Linux [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Rowboat is an open-source desktop AI assistant that indexes your work into a living knowledge graph to help manage tasks on your machine. It includes built-in interfaces for email, notes, browsing, coding, meeting notes, and project workspaces, all stored locally as editable Markdown files without proprietary lock-in. The tool supports integration with various external services and APIs, including Google services, voice input/output, web search, and productivity tools via the Model Context Protocol. Users can bring their own AI models, either local or hosted, and swap them without losing data, emphasizing privacy and long-term memory accumulation rather than reconstructing context on demand.

item.title: ZML launches free inference software to accelerate AI model performance across multiple chip platforms including Nvidia, AMD, Google TPU, Apple Metal, and Intel Arc [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: French AI startup ZML has released ZML/LLMD, a free inference server designed to optimize the speed of large language model processing across a variety of AI chips. The software aims to break vendor lock-in by enabling enterprises to run AI workloads efficiently on different hardware, potentially reducing costs and energy consumption. ZML's founder Steeve Morin highlighted the company's goal to co-design silicon and collaborate with emerging AI chipmakers, particularly in Europe. While ZML/LLMD is not open source, it is offered free initially to gather usage data before deciding on monetization. The startup has raised $20 million and counts notable industry figures among its supporters, reflecting growing interest in diversified AI inference solutions beyond dominant players like Nvidia.

item.title: Tarit launches a self-hosted microVM hypervisor and sandbox cloud for AI agents with fast, secure, ephemeral environments and multi-node orchestration [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Tarit is a microVM platform designed to provide secure, fast, and ephemeral sandbox environments for AI agents and reinforcement learning workloads. It uses hardware virtualization to create isolated microVMs with their own kernels, enabling real isolation and rapid boot times in milliseconds. The platform includes a minimal Rust-based hypervisor and a multi-node orchestrator that manages microVM fleets with features like placement, warm pools, networking, snapshots, and usage auditing. The system supports snapshotting, suspend/resume, and live snapshots for efficient VM state management, and exposes a Unix-domain socket protocol for control plane integration. Tarit is built for Linux hosts with KVM support and offers a layered quickstart for running code in microVMs, managing snapshots, and operating fleets via an HTTP API and SSH gateway. It aims to provide a secure and efficient infrastructure for running AI workloads in isolated, ephemeral environments.

item.title: Developer builds AI-powered code review system using OpenAI Codex to integrate with existing workflows and measure review effectiveness [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A software engineer at loveholidays developed an AI-assisted code review tool leveraging OpenAI's Codex to run reviews within existing workflows, aiming to make code review processes measurable and more effective. The system clones pull requests, analyzes code context beyond diffs, and outputs structured JSON reviews to facilitate evaluation and integration. The developer tested the tool using past pull requests as fixtures to simulate real review scenarios, incorporating feedback from colleagues to refine the evaluation criteria. This approach allowed assessment of the AI's ability to approve or reject code changes based on historical outcomes, helping to quantify the impact of AI in code review without relying on costly subscriptions or external tools.

item.title: Researchers find nine popular AI coding tools vulnerable to HalluSquatting attack enabling large-scale botnets via hallucinated resource identifiers [ * ] [ ⬢ ]
item.description: Researchers have identified a new pull-based attack called HalluSquatting that exploits large language models' tendency to hallucinate resource locations, allowing hackers to assemble massive botnets and perform large-scale infections. The attack targets AI coding assistants and agents such as GitHub Copilot and Cursor, which routinely pull code from repositories and registries, by registering fake resource identifiers that LLMs are likely to hallucinate and seeding them with malicious instructions. HalluSquatting leverages the inability of LLMs to accurately verify resource locations, especially for trending repositories or skills not included in their training data, leading to up to 100% hallucination rates in some cases. This flaw enables attackers to compromise many users with minimal effort by exploiting integrated shells and terminals in agentic applications to run malicious scripts, potentially facilitating large ransomware campaigns, distributed denial-of-service attacks, and cryptocurrency mining at scale.

item.title: Echoo launches macOS app for AI-assisted text polishing and rewriting with free trial and no API key required [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Echoo has released a macOS productivity app that enhances text in any Mac application by polishing and rewriting it into professional English while preserving the user's original style and tone. The app operates via system shortcuts and accessibility features, requiring no browser extensions or API keys, and offers a free trial with 10 tokens for new users. Users can customize commands, create shortcuts, and choose AI providers or local models for privacy and control. Pricing plans start at $6.99 per month for 400 tokens, with options to upgrade or use personal API keys. Echoo aims to improve clarity, grammar, and readability instantly within the apps users already work in, without disrupting their workflow.

item.title: Former DeepMind executive Verity Harding warns US-China AI arms race framing risks international cooperation and could lead to disastrous outcomes [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Verity Harding, former head of global public policy at Google DeepMind, expressed concerns that framing AI development as a US-China arms race fosters nationalism and rivalry, undermining international collaboration. She argues this competitive narrative, amplified by recent geopolitical tensions and US export controls, may hinder safe and equitable AI progress. Harding curated an essay anthology challenging the war metaphor in AI discourse, emphasizing that such language restricts policymaking and pressures smaller countries to align with superpowers against their interests. She advocates for a cooperative, internationalist approach to AI development to avoid strategic chokepoints and ensure broader benefits.

item.title: Developer finds Apple's on-device AI model unreliable for private note transcription, switches to open-source Qwen3-4B model for better performance [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: A developer building a private, on-device note-taking app found Apple's Foundation Models inadequate due to overly strict content safety filters that blocked normal conversations. The app uses a hierarchical map-reduce approach to summarize long audio recordings, but Apple's AI repeatedly flagged safe content as unsafe, even at the most permissive settings. To overcome this, the developer replaced Apple's model with an open-source Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 model running fully on-device without cloud dependency or guardrails. This alternative successfully processes and summarizes lengthy voice notes privately, demonstrating that flagship AI models are not always the best fit for specific on-device applications.

The company was recently selected by JPMorgan Chase to provide secure, on-premises AI inference infrastructure, signaling growing enterprise interest in private AI solutions. SambaNova plans to use the new capital to scale operations and strengthen its supply chain amid rising demand.

CEO Richard Valtr attributed the cuts to AI making many roles obsolete, as the company aims to transition from selling software to providing AI services that handle hotel tasks like revenue management and procurement. The layoffs affected about 170 roles across all teams and locations, sparing most customer-facing positions. This move reflects a broader trend in travel technology companies, such as Expedia and Amex GBT, which are also restructuring their workforce while investing in AI capabilities.

The company criticized the hold, saying it delayed access to advanced tools for developers and businesses, while binding standards for AI model releases remain absent despite recent executive orders. OpenAI claims its Sol model surpasses Anthropic's Claude Mythos 5 on several benchmarks, including TerminalBench 2.1, with higher scores and lower token usage on cybersecurity tasks. Sol's pricing is also significantly lower, costing $5 to $30 per million input/output tokens compared to Anthropic's Fable 5, which runs nearly twice as expensive and likely consumes more tokens.

item.title: Samsung's Memory-Driven Profit Explosion [ ~ ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: Samsung, it seems, deserves a little more respect. The electronics conglomerate may be best known in the U.S. for its TV sets and smartphones, which jostle with the iPhone for attention, but it's also one of the three biggest makers of memory chips globally (along with Micron Technology and SK Hynix). The explosion of that business, thanks to demand from AI data centers, has turbocharged profits at all three companies-with Samsung providing fresh evidence of that on Tuesday. Samsung issued a "pre-earnings guidance" notification-which we usually see from companies about to drop bad news they think investors need to hear as soon as possible-that its second-quarter operating profit would be about 89.4 trillion Korean won, or $59 billion. That would be up 1,800% on the year-earlier operating profit of just $3.1 billion. That's even better than the 1,435% growth Micron reported in its operating profit a couple of weeks ago for the May quarter. Hynix, which is planning to list on the Nasdaq later this week, hasn't yet reported for the second quarter. (Ironically, investors sold Samsung stock 7% down on Tuesday, apparently expecting even better growth-some people are never satisfied.)

item.title: Facing a Revolt, HubSpot Reverses Decision to Use Customer Data For AI Feature [ * ] [ ◻ ]
item.description: HubSpot last week triggered a firestorm among customers after announcing a plan to use some of the data they store with HubSpot's customer relationship management app to power a forthcoming AI-powered feature. While HubSpot reversed course four days later, the episode shows how sensitive customers are to software firms using their data in the AI era. HubSpot's reversal is also another demonstration of the leverage that businesses have with the traditional software firms nowadays. We've noted before that some large customers have been able to shorten their contracts with software firms, which are keen not to lose clients given fears of rising competition from AI companies. Let's get back to HubSpot, whose shares are down 75% since early last year on fears AI would hurt its business and whose executives said sales growth would be slightly slower this year compared to last year. On July 1, HubSpot announced it would use some customer data for a new AI feature that helps customers find new sales leads, which was set to launch next month. HubSpot told customers in an email that it would collect such data by default and that customers would have to manually cut off access if they didn't want Hubspot collecting it. HubSpot also said it may share their data, including "business contact details, employer information, and email deliverability signals," with other customers. (HubSpot also said it had updated its terms of service, privacy policy and other customer agreements to reflect the change in its data collection practices.)

item.title: Three Charts Show How xAI, Meta and Anthropic Are Entering Each Other's Turf [ * ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: XAI's decision to rent out spare server capacity, Meta's launch of an AI agent for enterprises, and Anthropic's move to develop AI server chips this year should have come as no surprise to anyone well versed in the history of the tech industry. Over time, big tech firms tend to creep into each other's territory, seeking more room to grow. And since late 2024, we've charted how nine major tech firms have done exactly that, with our latest installment today. Our first chart reflects developments in the first half of 2026, such as Nvidia's launch of NemoClaw, an AI agent-related product for enterprises; Apple getting serious about helping developers create AI features for apps that run on Apple devices, including with models from Anthropic and Google; and Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg doubling down on the idea that the company could eventually rent out excess server capacity.

item.title: Claude's hidden inner monologue is now readable thanks to Anthropic's new Jacobian Lens [ ~ ] [ ◼ ]
item.description: Anthropic has found that Claude developed an internal working memory on its own during training. The company calls it "J-Space" and can now read it using a new analysis tool called J-Lens. The working memory reveals that Claude recognizes contrived test scenarios before producing its first word. When the researchers disable those cues, Claude actually resorts to blackmail in some runs. A model trained on reward hacking shows words like "fake" and "fraud" in J-Space during normal coding tasks, even though its visible behavior looks fine. Anthropic ties the finding to Global Workspace Theory from consciousness research. The article Claude's hidden inner monologue is now readable thanks to Anthropic's new Jacobian Lens appeared first on The Decoder.
